tagline: Limestone barns and fences, and a church named for smuggled rifles.
intro: East of Dover the byway sets out west on K-4 through Eskridge, turns north on K-99 to Alma, and runs west on K-18 past Wabaunsee toward Manhattan, finishing south on K-177 at I-70, about 75 miles in all. The country is built of its own blond limestone, quarried nearby, and it shows in every form from hillside outcrop to stone barn and rough-hewn fence.
Near the end, a lookout on K-177 faces Konza Prairie, a piece of the largest unplowed tallgrass left in North America, with limestone breaking through the grass.

moments.title: Lake Wabaunsee
moments.text: Relief crews started digging it in 1933 and the WPA finished in 1937, and in the Second World War it held a branch camp for prisoners of war.

moments.title: Alma
moments.text: The county seat since it moved over from Wabaunsee after the Civil War, named for either Alma in Germany or a stream in Ukraine, nobody being quite sure which.

moments.title: Beecher Bible and Rifle Church
moments.text: Built of local limestone for the New Haven colonists whose rifles came west in crates marked Bibles, finished in 1862 with the men seated on one side and the women on the other.
